overview: White offers the g-pawn with 3.g4, hoping to open the g-file and the kingside against the Dutch. If Black takes with 3...fxg4 4.h3 gxh3 5.Bxh3 White gets some development and pressure on the light squares; 3...Nxg4 4.e4 is another try. Black generally keeps the extra material and returns it when needed. The attack is risky because White's own king has no pawn cover.

white_ideas.idea: Open the g- and h-files with h3 and aim Bxh3 and Qd3 or Qd2
Build a centre with e4 and use the lead in development

black_ideas.idea: Accept the pawns and consolidate with ...d5 and ...e6
Counter in the centre with ...e5 or ...d5 while White's king side is open

typical_structures.structure: Open kingside with the g-file exposed, Black ahead in material and White in development

character.notes: Early g4 creates immediate tactics around both kings.

gambit.notes: After 3...fxg4 Black can keep a pawn; 4.h3 gxh3 5.Bxh3 only partly regains it.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious: White weakens the king and Black can keep the pawn.

structure.notes: Kingside files open, centre not yet resolved.

level.notes: Few moves to learn but not a recommended repertoire line.

sublines_that_differ.name: Spielmann with 3...Nxg4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. g4 Nxg4 4. e4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black takes with the knight and White attacks in the centre.

character.reason: A pawn sacrifice and open g-file make the game double-edged from move three.

gambit.reason: White offers the g-pawn and Black can keep the material.

soundness.reason: White's king is weakened and Black can hold the pawn.

structure.reason: The kingside files open fast, though the centre is still undecided.

approach.reason: Strong players rarely play 3.g4 against the Dutch.

level.reason: A dubious line cannot be Beginner, and it has little deep theory.

plans.reason: The point is a direct attack on the kingside for the pawn.
